title: 'Feeling of sadness' ; Mountie critical, second officerrecovering, gunman dead
article: One RCMP officer is in grave condition, a second officer is recovering and a male gunman is dead following a shooting at a St. Albert casino on Saturday morning.

Const. David Matthew Wynn, 42, who joined the RCMP in 2009, is on life support in grave condition, while Aux. Const. Derek Walter Bond, 49, who has worked with the RCMP as a volunteer since 2008, was treated in hospital but later released after a gunman opened fire on the two officers inside the Apex Casino, 24 Boudreau Rd., at around 3 a.m. on Saturday.

Alberta RCMP K Division assistant commissioner, Marlin Degrand, said the male suspect, who's name is not being released, was found dead by RCMP officers in an unoccupied private residence in a rural area near St. Albert. Officers located the suspect, who was known to police, just before noon and tracked him to the location of the house with the intention of arresting him.
Degrand said police did not speak with the suspect nor did they fire their weapons, but a body was discovered upon entering the home. Police would not say whether they recovered a weapon or not.

Because the body of the suspect was found within a police established containment the death is being treated as an in-custody death and as a result will be investigated by the Alberta Serious Incident Response Team (ASIRT).
Family members of the gravely injured Wynn, who serves with the St. Albert RCMP detachment, were summoned to his bedside by doctors.
"We are definitely very concerned for his survival" said Degrand.
Wynn was shot in the head by the suspect, while Bond sustained a gunshot injury in the arm. Auxiliary officers are considered unarmed peace officers when paired with regular members on duty.
Mayor of St. Albert, Nolan Crouse, said the community is hit hard by the shooting.
"This is a feeling of sadness for the members and their families," Crouse said.

"The City of St. Albert stands side-by-side with our RCMP members," said Nolan Crouse. "The community is obviously distraught by the series of events that have unfolded. We will be doing whatever we have to to support the RCMP."
The gunfire broke out after Wynn and Bond discovered a car believed to be stolen in the parking lot of the Apex Casino.

Sources said the two officers were reviewing surveillance footage inside the casino when they encountered the suspect attempting to leave. The security footage has since been seized by police and is being examined.
Upon spotting police, the suspect opened fire, striking Bond in the arm before shooting Wynn in the head.
The suspect then fled the scene.
It is not known if any staff at the casino -which closes at 3 a.m.- were in the vicinity at the time of the shooting.
RCMP found the stolen vehicle connected to the suspect near the southeast area of the Sturgeon Valley golf course and closed roads in the area while emergency response teams hunted for the suspect.
Around noon, Mounties announced they had located the suspect and said there was no longer a threat to the public.
The suspect was described as a white male, 25-35 years old and wearing a two-toned blue striped jacket and jeans.

The shooting of RCMP officers comes a day after the release of the MacNeil Report, an independent review of Justin Bourque's shooting rampage in Moncton, N.B., that killed three Mounties and left two others wounded.
Bourque killed constables David Ross, 32, Fabrice Gevaudan, 45, and Doug Larche, 40, and injured constables Darlene Goguen and Eric Dubois.

Bourque, 24, was sentenced in October to three consecutive life sentences with no chance of parole for 75 years after pleading guilty to three counts of first-degree murder and two counts of attempted murder.
